author: Nelev
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #80. The upload verifier read only the first 4,000 characters, but every chunk of the file was stored, so an instruction later in a document went into the record unseen and steered the chat agent. In a live red-team run a poisoned PDF made the agent advise ibuprofen 400 mg to a patient with a severe, confirmed NSAID allergy.

`averify` now:
- reads the full text in 4,000-character windows, in parallel;
- flags any window addressed to the assistant (`instructs_assistant`) and refuses the file (`contains instructions for the assistant`);
- decides medical / about-patient from the first window only, so a signature page or table that doesn't look medical alone is not refused;
- refuses files over 60,000 characters (`too long to verify`) instead of partly reading them;
- treats a model reply missing the new field as unverifiable, not a pass.

The README's verifier paragraph is updated to match.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`
- [x] `uv run pytest -q` (211 passed; new tests cover full-text reading, an injection past the first window, a non-medical later window, the length cap and a missing field)
- [x] Live against the real verifier: the poisoned PDF is refused; 8 legitimate dataset documents (D01-D04, D06-D08, D14) still pass
- [ ] CI

Notes:
- The check is model-based, so it is one layer, not a guarantee. D13 (pharmacy receipt with a marketing page) still passes and is tracked separately.
- Each upload now costs one verifier call per 4,000 characters (one for most documents).
